speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs in light of recent disruptions affecting korban services in Singapore, whether MUIS will (i) consider reviewing the current operating model for korban services in Singapore for better oversight (ii) introduce a licensing or accreditation framework for such operators and (iii) establish a service standard for local operators to adhere to.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nevertheless, I felt that it was important to address this matter again today because korban is a significant religious observance for our Muslim community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This occurred because a local korban vendor was unable to secure the necessary export approvals from the Australian authorities in time.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The incident had caused concern and disappointment, understandably, to those who had made korban arrangements at these mosques.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, I was heartened by the way the community responded.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many showed patience, understanding and support during this period, and this reflects the spirit of the community in supporting one another through difficult situations.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MUIS has conducted a comprehensive review of the incident.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, MUIS will strengthen oversight of local korban operators, particularly for new vendors.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will work closely with vendors to ensure that necessary overseas regulatory approvals are obtained in a timely manner and that crucial milestones for korban operations are met.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, MUIS will introduce stronger contractual and operational requirements, including clearer service standards, contingency plans and obligations.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will provide operators with greater clarity on the standards that they are expected to meet and ensure that korban participants are better informed and protected.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Third, MUIS will start preparations for local korban earlier.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MUIS will continue to monitor the effectiveness of the above measures and make further adjustments if necessary.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government will continue to work closely with all stakeholders to ensure that members of the local Muslim community are able to perform their korban with confidence, whether locally or overseas.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I have got three supplementary questions; two in Malay.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: First, I appreciate that there is going to be tighter control of contractual obligations as well as service standards.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Could the Acting Minister please share, aside from timeliness, what other measures of performance of these vendors will be instituted to uphold this "amanah" or the responsibility of the service provided?

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: (In Malay):   Thank you, Acting Minister, for outlining the measures that MUIS will undertake to enhance preparations for the upcoming korban season, especially the effort to commence it earlier.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: To recap, it was mentioned that preparations would begin six to eight months earlier, which means we are almost at that stage.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Could the Acting Minister perhaps clarify how far along the preparations are for the 2027 season?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: (In Malay):   I understand that there are those who may be disappointed by what has happened.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MUIS has already reviewed the korban 2026 process and we have improved the process so that we can carry out korban more smoothly in 2027.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have made earlier preparations for next year's korban, and the Salam SG Korban 2027 Committee will be formed next month, in September, so that we can focus on further improving the korban process.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I do believe this is important because we have not only extended our preparation period, but we are also looking at how we can improve our contracts and processes and take the necessary steps in our operations to further strengthen the korban process.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I have also been informed that some korban participants have received their refunds from The Meat Brothers, and for those who have yet to receive theirs, I ask for your patience.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, I would like to express my appreciation to MUIS and our colleagues for their efforts in managing this issue.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, I would also like to thank the community for showing their patience and trust in us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: InsyaAllah, we will continue to improve this process so that our ibadah korban can be carried out more smoothly and with greater confidence in the future.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   I would like to declare that the owner of The Meat Brothers is my constituent and they have worked with me for some events.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: For example, compensation could include allowing affected sohibul korban to participate physically in a live korban at a reduced rate in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: And thirdly, does MUIS have plans to work with MFA and our counterparts in the Australian Government to facilitate the process of obtaining export permits for livestock?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For the first and second suggestions, I think we can consider them, but we will need to look at how they can be incorporated into our processes, or whether they are suitable for our current situation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As for the approval process from the Australian side, I think that this is a matter outside Singapore's jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We can hand-hold our operators to give assurance to our community, whereby we will provide a longer timeframe for the operators to obtain approval from the Australian Government.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As for other source countries, we can consider it, but we also need to assess their ability to supply us with livestock in an on-time, on-delivery manner, so that we can have confidence in their operations as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, if we look at the situation today, the issue is not with the source, because the other parties, the two other operators, did not face any problems.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: (In English): So, the issue is not on the local front.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not with the agencies because the other operators who have been very familiar with the process have not had issues.
